items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Evercold Preorders Are Now Live, Includes Standard & Collector's Editions
items.summary: Square Enix has launched preorders for Final Fantasy XIV Evercold, which arrives in February 2027. Get more details here.
items.content:
Pre-orders for the Standard and Collector’s Editions of the Final Fantasy XIV expansion, Evercold, have gone live ahead of its highly anticipated launch on February 23, 2027. You can purchase it as a collector’s bundle, which includes a digital version of the game but only on PC, which is a little odd considering the whole point of no disc was to include digital codes for the other systems. The Collector’s Box, which is just the physical merchandise, has also launched. At the time of writing, the EU/UK versions are now live, with the NA store getting the box added later on in the day at 10AM PST.

The bundles in the UK are £239.99 for the Collector’s Box and £289.99 for the Collector’s Bundle, which for some reason is a different button for PC/MAC, so make sure you pick the correct one. Also, this is not a Steam code. If you are on a PC and wish to purchase the Steam version, make sure to buy the box and then buy the Collector’s Edition separately.

In addition, the console versions are sold separately too, so you will need to visit the PSN Store if you wish to purchase the standard or collectors edition of Evercold. However, note that the licence for the game is not shared, and you will need to purchase the expansion on any platforms you play on, the items are so you only need to purchase the Collectors Edition once if you do own the game on several platforms.

The digital collectors edition that you get when either buying the bundle or on its own, will include the following:

If you preorder any edition before February 23, you will gain access to the following:

If you get the pre-order in, then you will gain access to Evercold around 9AM GMT (subject to change also please convert to your local timezone) on February 19, rather than February 23. The earring also continues the trend of EXP increasing items; this item will give you +30% EXP from enemies you defeat as you level up to 100. Plus, the Wind-up Köttr Minion I feel like is going to be a fan favourite with a heap of players simply due to how adorable it is. For more details on Everrcold, be sure to check out our recent Fanfest coverage here.

A new report has surfaced claiming that Ubisoft has delayed Assassin’s Creed Hexe internally, which could result in the game not coming out until 2028.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold confirms Zephyr class, new areas, new gearing, and a delay to February 2027
Final Fantasy XIV Evercold Delayed, New Release Date Announced at FFXIV Fan Fest
items.summary: The MMORPG's next expansion was set to launch shortly after the new year, but Warriors of Light will have to wait a bit longer.
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV Evercold was set to launch sometime in January 2027, which was announced as part of its initial reveal back in April this year during the North American FFXIV Fan Fest. However, this next expansion for the critically acclaimed MMORPG has been delayed – FFXIV Evercold's release date is now February 23, 2027 (and February 19, 2027 for early access). This was announced alongside the new, full trailer / intro cinematic for Evercold at FFXIV Fan Fest in Japan, and was said to only be a four-week delay.

In typical FFXIV fashion, the third and final teaser trailer is the full opening cinematic for an expansion, and it kicked off the Japan Fan Fest keynote where director and producer Naoki Yoshida presented more details on new features, where the ongoing story is headed, and fundemental gameplay changes as FFXIV goes into version 8.0 alongside Evercold's launch.

Pre-orders for Evercold open on November 4, 2026 and will come with a Wind-up Kottr minion to summon and follow you around in the world and Halone's Earring which will boost the EXP you gain for Jobs under level 100 when equipped. The collector's edition comes with the Valhallar Odin mount, the Entreat Crystal emote, and the Crystal Skyltborg which looks like glam for the new Bastion Job's weapons. The physical collector's bundle has the Evercold art book, the Tapestry of the Fourth decoration, a Kottr plush, a keychain of the Ethos Metal, and the Warrior of Light Reaper figure.

Additionally, we got a glimpse of the second new Job coming to his new expansion. It's a ranged DPS called Zephyr, which rocks a crossbow as their primary weapon and commands an avian companion to provide support.

There's a lot coming to FFXIV Evercold in addition to a new world and main story including a Neon Genesis Evangelion crossover raid series (which got a new teaser trailer) , a Final Fantasy VII crossover raid series, a new Tank Job with Bastion, and much more. Be sure to check out my Dawntrail review as well to look back at the last expansion before heading into this new era for FFXIV.

Michael is reviews editor at IGN and regularly contributes with previews, interviews, live events coverage, and news all in written and video form. He's usually entrusted with covering long RPGs and tech products, but he's got range when it comes to games. You'll also catch him at conventions and hosting video content, including IGN's weekly podcast Unlocked .

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold expansion delayed to February 23, 2027
items.summary: Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold, the patch 8.0 expansion for Final Fantasy XIV, will launch on February 23, 2027—a delay from its previously planned January 2027 release window—Square Enix …
items.content:
Sal Romano Oct 31 2026 / 12:25 AM EST 0 Final Fantasy XIV Online [11 articles]" href="https://www.gematsu.com/games/final-fantasy-xiv-online">Final Fantasy XIV : Evercold , the patch 8.0 expansion for Final Fantasy XIV , will launch on February 23, 2027—a delay from its previously planned January 2027 release window— Square Enix [5,507 articles]" href="https://www.gematsu.com/companies/square-enix">Square Enix announced. Early access will begin on February 19, 2027. Pre-orders will open on November 4.

A Collector’s Edition will also be available, which includes a Reaper figure, Ethos metal keychain, Kottr mini plush, “Tapestry of the Fourth,” and an Evercold special art box.

During the opening keynote, Producer and Director Naoki Yoshida [46 articles]" href="https://www.gematsu.com/people/naoki-yoshida">Naoki Yoshida revealed “Zephyr,” the second of two new jobs arriving in Evercold . A physical ranged DPS, zephyr joins the fray using a combination of crossbow shots and support from an avian familiar known as Nephele.

The keynote also introduced the full-length trailer for Evercold .

Alongside the release date, Yoshida revealed that pre-orders for the Evercold expansion and the previously announced Collector’s Box will start beginning Wednesday, November 4, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. PT / 1:00 p.m. ET.

The Collector’s Bundle will be available for pre-order in limited quantities exclusively from the Square Enix Store and contains the physical Collector’s Box and a code for the Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold Digital Collector’s Edition for Windows or Mac. PS5 [13,419 articles]" href="https://www.gematsu.com/platforms/playstation/ps5">PlayStation 5 , PS4 [29,144 articles]" href="https://www.gematsu.com/platforms/playstation/ps4">PlayStation 4 , Xbox Series [10,241 articles]" href="https://www.gematsu.com/platforms/xbox/xbox-series">Xbox Series X|S , Switch 2 [2,154 articles]" href="https://www.gematsu.com/platforms/nintendo/switch-2">Nintendo Switch 2 , and Steam players can order the Collector’s Box as a standalone product and pre-order the Evercold Digital Collector’s Edition separately on their respective platforms.

The Evercold Collector’s Box includes the physical goods listed below and does not include a copy of Evercold, in-game items, or pre-order bonuses.

Additionally, the Evercold Digital Collector’s Edition will include the following in-game items:

❮ ❯ Players who pre-order Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold from participating retailers will be eligible to receive the following bonuses:

Pre-order bonuses will be registered automatically for purchases made through the Mog Station, PlayStation [51,634 articles]" href="https://www.gematsu.com/platforms/playstation">PlayStation Store, Microsoft Store, and Nintendo [25,257 articles]" href="https://www.gematsu.com/platforms/nintendo">Nintendo eShop, with no separate pre-order code required. Purchases made through select retailers will grant a pre-order bonus code that can be redeemed immediately. As the in-game items will be delivered immediately upon pre-order, players can take advantage of the Halone’s Earring EXP bonus from defeating monsters through level 100 ahead of the release of Evercold.

A new trailer for the “EVANGELION: Ghosts of Desire Alliance” raid crossover was also revealed, alongside the announcement of new high-difficulty 8-player battles featuring select bosses from the alliance raid to create more challenging, savage-like eight-player encounters.

A new piece of artwork created by Final Fantasy VII Remake [107 articles]" href="https://www.gematsu.com/games/final-fantasy-vii-remake">Final Fantasy VII Remake series creative director Tetsuya Nomura was revealed alongside information on the newest difficulty option for raid encounters. The “Fierce” difficulty will fall between Normal and Savage difficulties currently available and will provide another avenue for an even wider range of players to experience the content.

Launches September 16, 2026, via Tokyo pop-ups and Diesel online.

Diesel has teamed up with Square Enix ‘s acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy XIV for a multi-faceted project anchored in the shared philosophy of “BRAVE”.

Fusing fashion, gaming culture and contemporary art, the centerpiece of the project is a 27-piece capsule collection. The lineup translates rich gaming lore into streetwear staples, spanning washed denim jackets, wide-leg denim trousers, hoodies, long-sleeve tees, graphic T-shirts and silver jewelry. Design motifs draw directly from the world of Hydaelyn, featuring imagery of Azem’s Crystal, the Mothercrystal, the Grand Companies of Eorzea and iconic Scions of the Seventh Dawn characters including Y’shtola, Thancred, Alphinaud, and Estinien.

Ranging in price from ¥11,000 to ¥207,900 JPY (approx. $69 – $1,302 USD), the collection kicks off on September 16, 2026, with an exclusive pop-up at Isetan Shinjuku in Tokyo, which will offer custom job-icon embroidery services and a 30-set limited “Scions of the Seventh Dawn Complete Box”. A wider release follows on October 2, 2026, via Diesel’s official online store and the DIESEL SHIBUYA flagship, alongside secondary pop-ups at Hankyu Umeda in Osaka and Iwataya in Fukuoka later in the month. Coinciding with the drop, DIESEL ART GALLERY in Shibuya will host a collaborative collage art exhibition by renowned artist Kosuke Kawamura from October 2 through November 8, 2026. items.title: Review: Final Fantasy XIV on Nintendo Switch 2 is the best version of the game
items.content:
I have wanted to get back into Final Fantasy XIV for quite some time. I am a massive fan of everything it offers, from the art direction to the scope of the world and adventures that are held within it. I love the way that it handles narrative within the MMO format, and the massive range of locations to visit. I really, really love the music (I went to a FFXIV symphony and everything), and just generally the very Final Fantasy design of it.

Related reading: To think that I played this for the first time way back on the PlayStation 3. My thoughts back then.

But – and it’s a big but – Final Fantasy XIV is a MMO, and MMOs do demand a time commitment, both in terms of the raw hours you plug into it, and the frequency with which you need to play. Take a big break from an MMO, and it just becomes progressively more difficult to step back into.

I tried to get back into FFXIV once when I first picked up the ROG Xbox Ally . The device handled the game just lovely, but I’m not a frequent PC player, and so at some point I put the device down, took a long break, and just… let my subscription slip again.

I am, however, a frequent Nintendo Switch 2 player. By that I mean “daily”. And so now, with the game’s little icon sitting right there on my Switch 2 home screen, I’ve been logging in for at least a little playtime every day. I’ve already made significantly more progress than I did on the ROG.

Final Fantasy XIV plays just lovely on Switch 2, to start with that important point. The console’s screen is just large enough to be able to handle the very busy interface (it’s an MMO, it’s necessary) without distracting from the core action when you want to watch the fireworks. The game’s visual engine is just now ever-so-slightly showing its age with relatively primitive character models and textures – it has been going for something like 13 years at this point – but the art direction is still as stunning as ever, and I’ve loved revisiting my favourite parts of the world from my first playthrough.

Speaking of, I have started a totally fresh character and save file (I wouldn’t even be able to track down my original avatar from a decade ago, if she still exists on servers somewhere, even if I wanted to. I can’t remember my username, password, or the email address it was attached to). I love how it’s possible to play through all the base game and early expansions with NPCs, and not rely on parties of humans for the various dungeons. If you’ve ever played a FFXIV dungeon before, you’ll know that human allies tend to… well, race through it. One of the few unpleasant memories I have from my first playthrough of Final Fantasy XIV was getting to the very final dungeon of the base game and basically missing the whole thing (and being left behind) because I was trying to follow the story. The conclusion to literally dozens of hours of play.

Now, thanks to NPCs, you can enjoy most of the many expansions and all the stories within them at your own pace. And enjoy the typically excellent music, enemy layouts and dungeon design without feeling rushed, too. I even took time to take screenshots, which is one of my favourite ways to log my adventures in this game.

There is a downside, though. Because Square Enix wants to funnel players into the later expansions where, from their perspective, all the value to the players is, they’ve taken steps to streamline the earlier parts of the game, meaning that you accumulate experience points much (much) faster, and have to do far (far) fewer quests along the way. I have been exclusively undertaking the main quest line, with no side quests, let alone grinding, and my avatar is more than twice the minimum recommended level for any given quest or boss battle.

I understand why they did this, because otherwise it would be a truly intimidating, overwhelming task for a completely new player to get up to the newer expansions, but it means that those same players don’t get to spend enough time in parts of the world to really enjoy their contribution to the whole. The major cities are fine, but you’ll fly through little town areas where previously you’d spend a gaming session or two completing all the side quests. They’re barely blips and blink-and-you’ll-miss-them moments now, which really messes with the pacing for what was previously a truly wonderfully paced game that slowly walked you from one wonder to the next.

I don’t necessarily know what the solution is there, though if it were possible, I would have appreciated the option to toggle whether I wanted the accelerating levelling on or not.

Still, that’s my only gripe. The only other minor issue is that, when it comes to the chat, the Switch’s virtual keyboard doesn’t exactly allow for the same typing speed as a proper keyboard. I don’t even know if it’s possible to connect a Bluetooth keyboard to the Switch 2, as I haven’t tried yet, but even if it were possible, that would significantly undermine the portability of the experience. Currently I haven’t been social enough in FFXIV to require the chat function much, but I can see that becoming an issue later on in the game.

Those are only minor quibbles, obviously, set against a game that is hundreds upon hundreds of hours in scope, and now in an extremely portable and accessible format. FFXIV is a hobby all by itself, and now I can embrace and indulge it in full.
